title: crypto2dev: errno-to-wolfSSL error mapping
description: Implement a shared crypto2dev_map_errno() function that translates Linux errno values returned by /dev/crypto2dev ioctls and read/write calls into wolfSSL error codes. Every algo handler calls this rather than translating inline. Mappings: -EACCES → CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE (FIPS gate not operational; soft failure, allow software fallback); -EBADMSG → AES_GCM_AUTH_E (GCM auth failure) or SIG_VERIFY_E (signature failure, per context); -EIO → WC_HW_E (session error state; hard failure, no fallback); -EINVAL → BAD_FUNC_ARG; -ENOMEM → MEMORY_E; -ENOENT → CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE (algo not registered; allow fallback); -EOPNOTSUPP → CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE (provider doesn't support op; allow fallback); -EMSGSIZE → BUFFER_E; -EBADF → WC_HW_E (logic error; hard failure). Implement in crypto2dev_port.c, declare in crypto2dev_port.h. Add static assert that WC_HW_E \!= CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE.
notes: Critical distinction: EACCES and ENOENT mean 'not available here, try software' (CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE). EIO means 'we started this operation on hardware and it is now broken' (WC_HW_E, hard fail). EBADMSG is auth failure — caller determines whether that maps to AES_GCM_AUTH_E or SIG_VERIFY_E based on context.
